prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: full-fidelity desktop portfolio landing-page direction comp, 1536 by 1024 landscape
Primary request: Design an actual responsive website viewport for COLTON SPURGIN as a candid cut-paper self-portrait, borrowing Alan Fletcher’s wit without copying a specific poster. The visitor must understand who Colton is, what he has done, and whether his working style fits them.
Scene/backdrop: no scene; flat front-facing website screenshot on warm paper
Subject: a personal portfolio for an Air Force NCO, lead software developer intern, research assistant, and UWF senior specializing in AI who graduates December 2026 and wants to build useful ambitious software before pursuing a master’s degree
Style/medium: high-fidelity web UI with torn paper blocks, wax-crayon marks, direct marker lettering, and deliberately imperfect alignment; candid and adult, not childish
Composition/framing: quiet top navigation with COLTON SPURGIN left and WORK, EXPERIENCE, ABOUT, CONTACT right; a two-column hero uses one enormous handwritten statement, “I BUILD SYSTEMS, LEARN HARD PROBLEMS, AND CARE ABOUT DOING USEFUL WORK WELL.” beside one abstract cut-paper shape made from four joined fragments; below it, four evidence scraps labeled AIR FORCE NCO, LEAD SOFTWARE DEVELOPER INTERN, RESEARCH ASSISTANT, and AI SPECIALIZATION · UWF · DEC 2026; show the beginning of SELECTED WORK with BORK, VELLM, TSP BENCHMARKS, HOME LAB. Make the personal statement the single dominant visual move and keep the rest orderly.
Color palette: warm paper #f5eedc, ink #171717, cobalt #1758b6, poppy #d84935, leaf #4d9848
Materials/textures: real torn paper edges, sparse crayon underline, marker lettering, light paper grain
Text (verbatim): “COLTON SPURGIN”; “WORK”; “EXPERIENCE”; “ABOUT”; “CONTACT”; “I BUILD SYSTEMS, LEARN HARD PROBLEMS, AND CARE ABOUT DOING USEFUL WORK WELL.”; “AIR FORCE NCO”; “LEAD SOFTWARE DEVELOPER INTERN”; “RESEARCH ASSISTANT”; “AI SPECIALIZATION · UWF · DEC 2026”; “SELECTED WORK”; “BORK”; “VELLM”; “TSP BENCHMARKS”; “HOME LAB”; “VIEW THE WORK”
Constraints: unmistakably a usable desktop website, not a poster; hierarchy and navigation must be legible; mature, direct, factual; no portrait photo; no logo; no invented employers, metrics, awards, testimonials, or project claims
Avoid: childish scrapbook, elementary-school craft aesthetic, generic portfolio cards, bento grid, neon cyber aesthetic, 3D mockup, browser chrome, illegible pseudo-text, gradients, rounded pill buttons, heavy shadows, watermark
